def: The combined iliacus and psoas major muscles, the main hip flexor. They insert on the lesser trochanter of the femur and are supplied by the femoral nerve and lumbar plexus.
Dormant, hardy spores formed inside some Gram-positive bacteria (Bacillus, Clostridium) that survive heat and disinfectants. Also the name for the spores inside a Coccidioides spherule.
Chains of elongated budding yeast cells that stay attached and resemble hyphae but have constrictions at the junctions. Candida albicans forms them.
Describes an organism that invades blood vessel walls, causing thrombosis and tissue infarction. Aspergillus and Mucor are angioinvasive molds in immunocompromised patients.
The replicating, noninfectious intracellular form of Chlamydia, which later condenses back into infectious elementary bodies.
Describes an antibiotic that inhibits bacterial growth rather than killing it, relying on the immune system to clear infection. Examples are macrolides, tetracyclines and clindamycin.
Treatment given in addition to the primary therapy to lower recurrence risk, such as chemotherapy after surgery. In vaccines it means a substance that boosts the immune response.
Describes injury or disease with impaired bile flow, with a predominant rise in alkaline phosphatase and conjugated bilirubin. Macrolides and amoxicillin-clavulanate can cause it.
The round, nonflagellated intracellular stage of Leishmania and Trypanosoma cruzi. They live and multiply inside macrophages or cells.
A hernia whose contents can be pushed back into the abdominal cavity. It contrasts with incarcerated and strangulated hernias, which cannot, and is a candidate for elective repair.
A fetal monitoring test that records heart rate accelerations with fetal movement. A reactive result is reassuring; a nonreactive one prompts further testing such as a biophysical profile.
A milk-filled cyst of the breast caused by a blocked duct, typically in lactating women or just after weaning. It presents as a soft, mobile, nontender mass.
Placing an endotracheal tube through the mouth into the trachea to secure the airway, using a laryngoscope.
An emergency surgical airway made by cutting through the cricothyroid membrane. It is used when intubation fails or is impossible.
Instillation of fluid into the uterine cavity during labor. It is used for oligohydramnios or variable decelerations from cord compression.
More than five uterine contractions in 10 minutes averaged over 30 minutes. It can be caused by oxytocin and may lead to fetal heart rate abnormalities.
Inflammation of a growth plate where a tendon attaches, from repeated traction in growing children. Osgood-Schlatter disease and Sever disease are examples.
Relating to the calcaneus, the heel bone. Calcaneal spurs and Achilles tendon insertion problems cause heel pain.
A rapid test for heterophile antibodies, used to diagnose infectious mononucleosis from Epstein-Barr virus. It can be falsely negative in children and in CMV mononucleosis.
Describes a drug bound to polyethylene glycol, which prolongs its half-life. Pegylated interferon-alpha treats hepatitis B and C.
Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), made by the anterior pituitary, which stimulates cortisol release from the adrenal cortex. Corticotropin-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus controls it.
Enlargement of the clitoris, a sign of virilization from androgen excess, as in congenital adrenal hyperplasia or androgen-secreting tumors.
The three-carbon intermediate of fatty acid synthesis made by acetyl-CoA carboxylase. It inhibits carnitine acyltransferase I, blocking fatty acid entry into mitochondria.
Neuroendocrine C cells of the thyroid that secrete calcitonin. They lie between follicles and give rise to medullary thyroid carcinoma.
Relating to meals. Preprandial and postprandial describe the times before and after eating, as in prandial insulin dosing.
Glucose in the urine, seen when blood glucose exceeds the renal threshold or with SGLT-2 inhibitors.
Relating to the myometrium, the smooth muscle layer of the uterus. Myometrial contraction is stimulated by oxytocin and prostaglandins.
Embryonic folds that become the labia majora in females and the scrotum in males.
Glands beside the female urethra (Skene glands), homologous to the male prostate.
Describes a swirling pattern of fibers, seen in leiomyoma (fibroid) cut surface and in meningioma and schwannoma histology.
A circular arrangement of cells around a central space. Examples are Homer Wright rosettes in neuroblastoma and Call-Exner bodies in granulosa cell tumors.
Blood collection beneath the capsule of an organ. In HELLP syndrome a hepatic subcapsular hematoma can rupture, causing hemorrhagic shock.
Conversion of fat into soap-like calcium salts. In fat necrosis of the breast or pancreas, fatty acids bind calcium, forming chalky deposits.
Describes fluid that is thin and watery mixed with blood, giving a pink tint, such as nipple discharge from intraductal papilloma.
Describes tissue that reflects fewer ultrasound echoes than its surroundings and appears darker. Solid masses are often hypoechoic.
Describes dense fibrous stromal reaction around a tumor, giving a hard texture. It is common in invasive ductal breast carcinoma and pancreatic cancer.
Describes thickened skin from excess keratin, producing scaly or horny plaques.
The back of the head. Prominent occiput is a finding in Edwards syndrome (trisomy 18).
An imaginary vertical line from the middle of the clavicle, used to locate findings such as the point of maximal impulse in the fifth intercostal space.
Relating to the layer just beneath the endocardium. It is most vulnerable to ischemia because it is farthest from epicardial arteries, so ST depression occurs.
Absence of movement. In the heart it describes a wall segment that fails to contract after infarction; in Parkinson disease it means difficulty initiating movement.
Describes degeneration with excess mucoid connective tissue. Myxomatous degeneration of the mitral valve causes prolapse.
A condition that results from a prior disease or injury, such as rheumatic heart disease after strep infection.
A class III antiarrhythmic that blocks potassium channels and prolongs the action potential. It converts atrial fibrillation or flutter but can cause torsades de pointes.
Vibration felt on the chest wall when the patient speaks. Tactile fremitus increases over consolidation and decreases with effusion or pneumothorax.
Essential fructosuria is a benign defect of fructokinase causing fructose in the urine. It is asymptomatic, unlike hereditary fructose intolerance.
A leukotriene receptor antagonist (CysLT1) used to prevent asthma and allergic rhinitis. Zafirlukast is the same class; neuropsychiatric effects are a warning.
Describes a chest imaging pattern of net-like lines with small nodules, seen in interstitial lung diseases, sarcoidosis and miliary spread.
A direct renin inhibitor that blocks conversion of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I. It lowers blood pressure and is contraindicated in pregnancy.
Units of solute that contribute to osmotic pressure. Milliosmoles per liter express plasma osmolarity.
The protein encoded by PKHD1. Mutations cause autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.
Low urinary citrate, which promotes calcium stone formation. It can be caused by metabolic acidosis and treated with potassium citrate.
A ceramide with one sugar attached. Glucocerebroside accumulates in Gaucher disease and galactocerebroside in Krabbe disease.
An essential activator of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I in the urea cycle. Its deficiency causes hyperammonemia.
A cofactor for phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan hydroxylases. Its deficiency causes a form of phenylketonuria and neurotransmitter deficiency.
When one hormone must be present for another to act fully. Cortisol permits catecholamine effects on blood vessels.
